tip: Stromend is a present participle, infinitive stromen plus -d, working like an adjective in stromend water.
Goedenavond is written as one word: goede plus a linking -n plus avond, a leftover old ending.
Te plus an infinitive shows purpose: hang de was te drogen means hang the laundry to dry.
After waarom the clause sends its verb to the end: de reden waarom hij vertrok.
After a number, a unit like kilometer stays singular: achttien kilometer, never achttien kilometers.
With a modal in the perfect, use the infinitive not the participle: had kunnen vermoeden, not had gekund.
Heel before an adjective means very: heel bijzonder is very special.
Wakker worden uses worden, to become, for a change of state: werd ik wakker means I woke up.
Aankomen is separable; in a main clause the aan drops to the end: kwamen wij aan, we arrived.
Kortom stands outside the sentence with a comma, so it skips inversion: Kortom, het was, subject stays first.
Je is the unstressed your as well as you: je weekend means your weekend; the stressed form is jouw.
Daarvoor fuses daar plus voor to mean before that; Dutch builds these daar-words instead of voor dat.
Ondanks is a preposition and takes a noun: Ondanks de regen. For a full clause use hoewel instead.
Vinden is a strong verb: the past changes the vowel to vond, plural vonden, not a -de ending.
Comparisons use dan, not als: anders dan verwacht means other than expected.
Pas before a time means not until: pas na middernacht is not until after midnight.
Leeg becomes lege before a noun; the doubled ee shrinks to one e because the syllable opens up.
Honderden with -en means hundreds, a vague large number; plain honderd would count exactly one hundred.
Nadenken here is an infinitive used as a noun: na lang nadenken, after long thinking.
Vlak before a preposition means right or just: vlak voor het examen is right before the exam.
Wat een plus a noun makes an exclamation of degree: Wat een mazzel means what luck.
Verte comes from the adjective ver, far, plus -te, the ending that turns adjectives into nouns.
Dag by itself means both hi and bye, an informal greeting or farewell, apart from dag meaning day.
Nauwelijks paired with a later of means barely had X happened when Y: Nauwelijks was ik thuis of de telefoon ging.
De was here is a noun, the laundry, and uncountable; it looks identical to was from wassen and zijn.
Het gaat prima uses impersonal het for wellbeing, literally it goes fine, the reply to hoe gaat het.
A modal like moet sends the main verb to the end as an infinitive: moet haar huiswerk afmaken.
The indirect object comes before the direct and needs no word for to: geeft hem een cadeautje.
Hun marks the indirect object them: Zij vertelt hun het verhaal, she tells them the story.
Weer here means again: komt weer terug, comes back again; the same word also means weather.
